subject: Audit & Access log export, retention, and deletion attestation — delivery/playbook
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@finvero.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Cc: compliance@finvero.com
Date: 2027-11-09 09:14 -0800
Subject: How can we get full audit + access logs exported (retention + deletion proof)?

Hi Lauren,

Quick question from the Finvero compliance team — we need a clear playbook for getting our tenant's audit and access trace exports for the last 3 years. Specifically:

- Export formats you can provide (NDJSON/CSV/parquet?) and whether payloads include request/response metadata.
- Typical delivery time for a full export of a single-tenant (approx 2.5B events).
- What proof you provide after a deletion request (audit trail/tombstone + signed attestation?).
- Any constraints around data residency and cross-border egress for exports.

Can you send a short runbook we can share with legal and IT, and an example manifest? We may need a signed export acceptance and proof-of-deletion step for our regulator.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Reed
Head of Compliance, Finvero
[Finvero]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@finvero.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: 2027-11-09 11:02 -0800
Subject: Re: How can we get full audit + access logs exported (retention + deletion proof)?

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a short delivery checklist and a sample manifest. I included Marissa and Karthik to cover handoff and key-management specifics.

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Formats: we can deliver exports as gzipped NDJSON (recommended for line-delimited event traces), CSV slices for legacy tooling, or parquet for analytics read-optimized delivery. Files are SHA256 checksummed and delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket or (for Private) an internal object store.
- Delivery time: for a dataset ~2.5B events we typically stage and chunk the export; first slice (most recent 90 days) within 72 hours, bulk completion depends on tenant size and routing — typically 2–7 business days for the full dataset. We provide progress updates and manifests with estimated completion timestamps.
- Proof of deletion: after an approved erase, Redwood emits a deletion manifest showing tombstone markers, S3 object removal confirmation, and a signed attestation (PGP) including SHA256 root of the manifest and deletion timestamps. For hosted tenants we also provide key-value tombstone markers and a purge-run report.
- Cross-border/residency: exports follow your tenant's residency policy. For US-region tenants we keep exports in the requested region unless you request cross-region delivery; for cross-border we can do encrypted transfer to an EU bucket but you'll need to accept the egress routing in writing.

Operational notes (details):
- Chunking: Exports are generated in time-sliced chunks (configurable window: hourly/daily). Each chunk file contains event-level metadata: event_id, timestamp, principal_id, action, resource_id, source_ip, region, outcome, and (if requested) request/response metadata.
- Integrity: Every file has a SHA256 and is listed in the top-level manifest.csv. We sign the manifest with an export-key (PGP) and can provide a signed SHA256 root hash for long-term attestation.
- Legal hold: If Finvero places a legal hold, files are retained and excluded from scheduled purge flows; we mark them immutable and flag them in the manifest. Legal-hold state requires an authorized internal ticket and may delay deletion proofs.
- Deletion cadence: For standard erase requests we begin the removal workflow within 24 business hours; S3 object deletions and tombstone replication finish within 72 hours. For archival tiers there may be an additional staging step (up to 7 days).

Attached: export-sample-manifest.csv (small sample), export-delivery-checklist.pdf.

Next steps: If that aligns, Marissa will coordinate the export window and Karthik will confirm KMS/transfer details. If you need a signed attestation template for your regulator we can draft it and route for signature.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example, Alex Reed <alex.reed@finvero.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: 2027-11-10 08:46 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit & Access log export, retention, and deletion attestation — delivery/playbook

Quick follow-ups from engineering operations:

- KMS/encryption: For hosted tenants we can deliver to your S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-S3) or with SSE-KMS (we can request a customer-managed key). For Redwood Private we can hand over an encrypted archive using your external KMS (KMS alias required).
- Transfer mechanics: We support direct PutObject to your bucket (recommended) or a temporary pre-signed URL scheme for very large customers. For very large exports we can ship encrypted multipart archives to Snowball/physical devices on request (rare).
- Residency flags: We tag each event with region and tenant-residency field; if the export crosses boundaries we include an export-declaration in the manifest to satisfy auditors.

Operational request for Finvero: please confirm
1) Destination(s) (S3 bucket ARN or contact for Private handoff),
2) Whether you require customer-managed KMS, and
3) If you have an active legal hold list (so we can exclude/mask).

I can stand up the export job once we have the above — expected scheduling lead-time 24 hours after confirmation for the initial slice.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Ops Engineer, Export Services
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@finvero.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Cc: compliance@finvero.com
Date: 2027-11-12 16:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit & Access log export, retention, and deletion attestation — delivery/playbook

Thanks — this looks good and much clearer than our first ask.

Finvero confirms:
- Destination: s3://finvero-compliance-exports (us-east-1). We'll provide bucket policy and an IAM role for Redwood to assume.
- KMS: We want SSE-KMS with our customer-managed key (alias/ARN to follow).
- Legal hold: No active holds for the requested range.

Please proceed with an initial slice covering 2027-08-01 -> 2027-11-09 (most recent 100 days) and provide the signed manifest + SHA256 root when the slice is ready. We'll then schedule the full backfill.

One ask about deletion attestation: can Redwood include a short signed statement with the manifest that includes: tenant-id, export-range, deletion-schedule (if erase requested), and a signed root-hash? Our regulator needs the statement signed by a senior security officer. If needed we can run a short PO or MSA amendment to include the attestation.

Appreciate the turnaround — Alex
Alex Reed
Head of Compliance, Finvero
